correctness.rationale: For each n>=4, 0<p<=1, p-triangle bounds produce two universal extensions, leaf and arithmetic center. Lower bound uses one isometric embedding into the finite real free p-space. Any center with negative barycentric coefficient is strictly worse than radius two by the F_p>=F_1 inequality. Theorem 2.2 finite tree costs show the exact positive-simplex norm 2^p sum_{j ne i} lambda_j^p, because rooted subtree flows dominate positive masses. The ordered simplex extreme points have k equal nonzero final coordinates, and concavity yields minimum min(1,(n-1)n^(-p)); strict concavity provides optimal-center classification for p<1, and p=1 is checked separately. The first public source and primary 46A16 status are shown in arXiv v1. Finite computer tests are corroborative only.

value.rationale: The universal one-point extension trace is an established natural invariant. The exact all-n formula describes a substantive phase transition between vertex and barycenter extremizers, shows p_n strictly increases to one, and proves an endpoint separation: for every fixed 0<p<1 sufficiently large finite stars reach sharp factor two while every finite star at p=1 has smaller trace. This complete infinite family classification improves the crude upper bound two and goes beyond an arbitrary small finite slice or the already known n=3 case.
